audit_notes: Model: shear-lag of a barnacle base plate (E_b t_b = 1e8*5e-4 = 5e4 N/m) bonded over its radius R to the coating through an interface of shear stiffness k (Pa/m); the hydrodynamic drag on the organism (tau_h*pi R^2) enters the base at its periphery as a line load F = tau_h R/2 = 0.5 N/m; interfacial shear = k u, peak at the edge x = 0. Analytical: tau_peak = F (lambda/R) coth(lambda), lambda^2 = k R^2/(E_b t_b). Design (hydration interface on hard PU, k = 1e10 Pa/m as proposed): lambda = 2.24, tau_peak = 0.5*447*1.02 = 229 Pa. Baseline: standard silicone foul-release film (G = 0.33 MPa, t = 0.3 mm) acting as the interface compliance, k = G/t = 1.1e9 Pa/m: lambda = 0.74, tau_peak = 118 Pa. RESULT: the design concentrates interfacial stress ~2x MORE than a standard silicone foul-release coating, i.e. a negative gain. Physical reason: a nm-thin layer on a hard substrate is elastically far stiffer than a 0.3 mm soft silicone film; k = 1e10 is already optimistic (an elastic hydration layer of G ~ 1e5-1e6 Pa over 5 nm gives 2e13-2e14 Pa/m). The only way the concept could work is true viscous sliding (hydration lubrication), which a steady elastic model cannot represent and which requires the fouler's cement not to penetrate or bind to the brush - cartilage works because both surfaces carry hydrated brushes, whereas barnacle cement is a cross-linked adhesive that displaces bound water. Parameters are physically possible; audit passed so that this honest negative result is recorded. Dimensionless: lambda (design) = 2.24, lambda (baseline) = 0.74, k_design/k_baseline = 9.1, hydrodynamic shear/typical release stress = 200/5e4 = 0.004.
